events.title: Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty Signed
events.description: The United States, the Soviet Union, and the United Kingdom signed the Partial Test Ban Treaty in Moscow, prohibiting nuclear weapons tests in the atmosphere, in outer space, and underwater.
events.significance: It was the first major nuclear arms control agreement of the Cold War, reducing radioactive fallout and paving the way for later arms limitation treaties.

events.title: Nelson Mandela Arrested
events.description: Anti-apartheid leader Nelson Mandela was arrested near Howick, South Africa, after 17 months on the run. He was later convicted of sabotage and related charges and sentenced to life imprisonment.
events.significance: His imprisonment of 27 years made him a global symbol of resistance to apartheid, and he later became South Africa's first democratically elected president.

events.title: Death of Marilyn Monroe
events.description: Actress and cultural icon Marilyn Monroe was found dead at her home in Los Angeles at age 36. Her death was ruled a probable suicide from a barbiturate overdose.
events.significance: Her death cemented her status as an enduring icon of Hollywood and American popular culture and sparked lasting public fascination.

events.title: First Electric Traffic Light Installed
events.description: The first electric traffic signal in the United States was installed in Cleveland, Ohio, at the corner of Euclid Avenue and East 105th Street, using red and green lights with a warning buzzer.
events.significance: It was an early step in modern traffic control, helping manage the growing number of automobiles and improving road safety in cities worldwide.

events.title: Ambato Earthquake in Ecuador
events.description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck central Ecuador near Ambato, destroying towns and triggering landslides that buried communities in the Andes.
events.significance: It was one of the deadliest earthquakes in the Western Hemisphere in the 20th century, killing about 5,000 people and shaping Ecuador's later approach to disaster response.
